_doc: Villagers' tastes (Tastes, scripts/systems/tastes.gd). Each villager likes some pieces and some paint colours. A piece they like, or a piece painted a colour they like, put up within `radius` metres of their spot (`near`: one of the layout's hangouts, or [x, z]) earns a heart and their `line` once a day ({piece} is the piece's name). The morning paper gives away one taste nobody has heard yet (`gossip`), and the bag lists the tastes you know. At an inauguration, a villager who likes a piece in what's opened cheers for it.

fern.line: Oh, a {piece}! You do know me.
fern.gossip: Overheard: Gigia can't walk past a hedge without patting it. Green paint makes her weep.

bram.line: A {piece}! Proper wiring, I hope. Lovely.
bram.gossip: Overheard: Elio stops to admire every lamp in the village, lit or not. Yellow is his favourite colour. He says it's 'the colour of current'.

percival.gossip: Overheard: the Sindaco believes every village needs more columns and statues. Red, he says, is the colour of leadership.

tilly.line: Ooh, a {piece}! That's going on the website.
tilly.gossip: Overheard: Fede photographs every sign and windmill for the website. Blue and lilac, she says, look best on a screen.

mabel.line: A {piece}! My customers will love it.
mabel.gossip: Overheard: Ornella wants benches and tables everywhere people might eat bread. Which is everywhere. And she adores pink.

captain.line: A {piece}, at my stop! Now that's a service.
captain.gossip: Overheard: Aldo would like a bench and a roof at every bus stop in the province. Painted bus blue, ideally.

river_town_ermes.line: A {piece}. Sensible. The river respects sensible.
river_town_ermes.gossip: Overheard: Ermes trusts anything that could stop a flood: sandbags, stone, railings, a good streetlight. Dark slate is the only honest colour, he says.

river_town_tullio.gossip: Overheard: in forty years Tullio has said more about pontoons and benches by the water than about anything else. He likes teal, like the river.

river_town_primo.line: A {piece}! Now that's something a cyclist can use.
river_town_primo.gossip: Overheard: Primo says a town is only as good as its streetlights and signposts for cyclists. And everything should be racing green.

river_town_gildo.line: A {piece}, right where I can watch for him.
river_town_gildo.gossip: Overheard: Gildo wants a bench and a lantern by the water, to watch for the monster. Brown, like an old boat.

river_town_mattia.gossip: Overheard: Mattia pretends not to care, but he stops for anything electric: lamps, windmills, signs. Light blue, if you ask.

river_town_wanda.gossip: Overheard: Wanda says every dance hall needs lamps, flowers and somewhere to swoon. Pink or lilac, never beige.

river_town_rina.line: A {piece}. More customers, more card games. Good.
river_town_rina.gossip: Overheard: Rina could always use more tables and chairs for the card players. Green, like the bar's awning.

river_town_ines.line: A {piece}. Poplar, I hope, and not a scrap wasted.
river_town_ines.gossip: Overheard: Ines likes honest woodwork: fences, wooden walls, tables, beams. Plain wood brown, of course.

river_town_pierina.line: A {piece}! A nice spot to stop for coffee.
river_town_pierina.gossip: Overheard: Pierina stops at every bench and flower bed on her round. Yellow, like her jacket.

rice_village_ernesto.line: A {piece}. Regulation, that. The railway would approve, if it ever came.
rice_village_ernesto.gossip: Overheard: Paletta says a proper station wants lanterns, an enamel sign and flower beds. Signal red and green, of course.

rice_village_battista.gossip: Overheard: Barba Tista only trusts things that keep water where it belongs: stone, fences, levers and pumps. Mud brown never shows the dirt, he says.

rice_village_pierina.line: Oh, a {piece}! In 1951 we'd have given an arm for one.
rice_village_pierina.gossip: Overheard: Nonna Pierina says the edge of a paddy wants flowers, trees and somewhere to sit. And bright pink, whatever her son says.

rice_village_silvia.line: A {piece}! That's what gets a mill turning.
rice_village_silvia.gossip: Overheard: Silvia lights up at anything with a gear in it: waterwheels, shafts, a good workbench. Rice-shoot green, she says, is the future.

rice_village_remo.line: A {piece}. Blessed, I'd say. Don't tell the bishop.
rice_village_remo.gossip: Overheard: Don Remo says a churchyard wants lamps, pillars and the odd statue. White and gold, like his Christmas vestments.

rice_village_matteo.line: A {piece}! I'm writing it down in my log.
rice_village_matteo.gossip: Overheard: Matteo wants railway things by the crossing: lanterns, signposts, enamel signs. Yellow, like the inspection train.

metropolis_augusto.line: A {piece}. The courtyard looks respectable again. Wipe your feet.
metropolis_augusto.gossip: Overheard: Augusto judges a courtyard by its benches, its flower beds and a proper sign. Courtyard-door green, he says, is the only colour for a respectable building.

metropolis_sala.line: A {piece}. Practical, and within budget, I trust.
metropolis_sala.gossip: Overheard: Ragioniere Sala respects anything you can file things in: cabinets, bookshelves, a good desk. And a streetlight saves on candles. Slate grey, like his suits.

metropolis_annoni.line: A {piece}. In marble it would last six hundred years. This will do for now.
metropolis_annoni.gossip: Overheard: the Architetto stops for statues, columns, arches and pillars, the way other people stop for gelato. White, like Candoglia marble.

metropolis_ambrogio.line: A {piece}! Passengers will wait in comfort. Ding ding!
metropolis_ambrogio.gossip: Overheard: Ambrogio wants every stop to have a bench, a sign and a light in the fog. Tram orange, of course.

metropolis_franco.line: A {piece}. Good for business. Have a coffee on the house.
metropolis_franco.gossip: Overheard: Franco would line the whole Naviglio with tables, chairs and counters if the city let him. Bitter red, like his aperitivo.

metropolis_chiara.line: A {piece}! It's like something out of a magazine.
metropolis_chiara.gossip: Overheard: Chiara can't walk past a rug, a painting or a good lamp without redesigning the room around it. Lilac or pink, darling.

metropolis_gino.line: A {piece}. Bravo! Bravissimo! It deserves an encore.
metropolis_gino.gossip: Overheard: Maestro Gino loves anything that would look good on a stage: lamps, lanterns, statues, paintings. Gilded yellow, like the opera boxes.

metropolis_ottavio.line: A {piece}. The park says thank you. So do I.
metropolis_ottavio.gossip: Overheard: Ottavio only trusts things that grow: trees, hedges, flower beds, a pond for the ducks. Leaf green, naturally.

metropolis_gennaro.line: A {piece}! Chestnuts taste better next to one of these.
metropolis_gennaro.gossip: Overheard: Gennaro says a good stall needs a counter, a roof, a lamp and somewhere to sit and eat. Chestnut brown, what else?

metropolis_rocco.gossip: Overheard: Rocco wants streetlights, signs, railings and somewhere high to stand, so the traffic behaves. White like his helmet, or police blue.

metropolis_vale.line: A {piece}! That's a photo. That's at least two inches!
metropolis_vale.gossip: Overheard: Vale writes up anything photogenic: signs, paintings, a desk to type at, a streetlight for night shots. Yellow, like the paper's masthead.

metropolis_simone.line: A {piece}. Structurally honest. My professor would cry.
metropolis_simone.gossip: Overheard: Simone can talk for an hour about a pillar, a column, a roof or a good stair. Teal, for some reason he calls 'modernist'.

metropolis_elvira.line: A {piece}! My late husband would have loved it.
metropolis_elvira.gossip: Overheard: Signora Elvira wants the courtyard full of flower beds, a tree, hedges and a bench in the sun. Rose pink, like her geraniums.

olive_village_giobatta.line: A {piece}! Civic. Dignified. I'll wear the sash for it.
olive_village_giobatta.gossip: Overheard: the Sindaco loves anything a town hall would put up: signs, statues, streetlights. Red is the colour of authority, he says, and of his barber's pole.

olive_village_klaus.line: A {piece}! It looks four hundred years old already. Wunderbar!
olive_village_klaus.gossip: Overheard: Klaus Wendt goes weak at the knees for old stonework: arches, columns, a good stone block. Terracotta orange is his favourite colour. He has photographed every roof.

olive_village_hannelore.line: A {piece}! Don't move it. Click. Perfect.
olive_village_hannelore.gossip: Overheard: Hannelore will photograph any painting, flower bed or lamp. Good light, she says. Sea blue is her colour. Her camera strap is sea blue too.

olive_village_bastian.gossip: Overheard: Bastian says 'mm' twice for trees, fences and garden paths. Twice is a lot. Green, olive green, is the only colour he trusts.

olive_village_gina.line: A {piece}! Wait till I tell everyone. I'll tell them now.
olive_village_gina.gossip: Overheard: Nonna Gina wants benches to sit and talk on, and flowers to talk about. White, she says, like clean washing.

olive_village_delia.line: A {piece}. Hm. It could have gone worse.
olive_village_delia.gossip: Overheard: Nonna Delia approves of stairs and railings: things that hold a person up. Dark slate is the only respectable colour, she says. She's worn it since 1971.

olive_village_rosa.line: A {piece}! For my customers. All six of them.
olive_village_rosa.gossip: Overheard: Rosa can't see a table, a chair or a counter without imagining it full of people eating. Rose pink, like her name.

olive_village_giacomo.line: A {piece}. Now that's useful. Like a good net.
olive_village_giacomo.gossip: Overheard: Gambero likes things a fisherman can use: benches to mend nets on, railings to lean on, a lantern on a post. Navy, dark as a night sea, is his colour.

olive_village_marisa.line: A {piece}! TOOT! Sorry. I toot for things I like too.
olive_village_marisa.gossip: Overheard: Sirena loves anything a port needs: signposts, streetlights, lanterns to steer by. White, like her ferry's hull.

olive_village_ilario.line: Mm. A {piece}. The bees hum about it.
olive_village_ilario.gossip: Overheard: Fuco wants flower beds, hedges and beehives, anything the bees would like. Broom yellow is his colour, like his honey.
